questions.question: The ____ trailer is most likely to tip over if a driver turns too quickly.
questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous. The last trailer is most likely to roll over.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than usual.
Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
Push the brake pedal more lightly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: With ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System), brake the same way you would without ABS. Use normal brake pressure.

questions.question: The emergency air line:

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake.
Is connected to the relay valves.
Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks on combination vehicles and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in the ____ position.
questions.explanation: On older vehicles, tractor protection controls may use levers instead of knobs. The "normal" position is correct for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: To test the tractor protection valve, a driver should:

options.text: Release air using the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air using the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve this way: Let the air supply charge fully. Turn off the engine. Press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to emergency position when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to jackknife, you should NOT:

options.text: Allow the wheels to grip the road.
Allow the trailer to straighten out.

questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels grip the road again. Do not apply the trailer hand brake. Brakes caused the wheels to lock, so using the hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) operates the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: A shut-off valve:

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Is located on the instrument panel.
Prevents air from escaping an air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents air from escaping an air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed. This stops air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: When crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for your vehicle.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. Wait for a large enough gap in traffic before entering or crossing.

questions.question: A trolley valve:

options.text: Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
Should be used when parking uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be used to test trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trolley valve (also called the trailer hand valve or Johnson bar) works the trailer brakes. Use it only to test brakes. Do not use it while driving—it can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking—it can release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from leaving air brake systems.
Stop air from entering air brake systems.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. Keep the rear shut-off valve closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Bobtail tractors are hard to drive and require extra caution.

questions.question: How does a fully-loaded rig compare to an empty rig in terms of rollover risk?

options.text: Just as likely to roll over.

questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity from the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes too quickly?

options.text: A crack-the-whip effect that causes a rollover.
Other drivers get confused about which lane you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crack-the-whip effect that causes a rollover.
questions.explanation: The crack-the-whip effect happens when you change lanes too fast in a combination vehicle. This can cause a rollover.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Leave the emergency line valve open.
Leave the rear shut-off valves open.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open both the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check for escaping air. Then close both valves before you start your trip.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, maintain a following distance of at least ____ for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?

options.text: It will not make a difference when coupling.

questions.explanation: Check the trailer height before coupling. If the trailer is too low, it can damage the trailer nose. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: If your trailer goes off course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Pull forward, readjust, and back again.
Get out and move the trailer by hand.
Turn the wheel all the way left until the trailer straightens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward, readjust, and back again.
questions.explanation: If your trailer goes off course while backing, pull forward and reposition your vehicle before continuing to back up.

questions.question: What is one function of the emergency air line?

options.text: Flash when air pressure is low.
Help control the vehicle in bad weather.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) supplies air to the trailer tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.
